description: The window.PLATFORM_ICONS value in site/data/platform-icons.js -- owned by vertex-order/platforms, vendored into kit and every list repo via sync.toml. `key` is what a series entry's platforms[].key looks up to merge icon/size/style/name in. Render-only props that a per-entry platforms item can also set (href, itemName, terminated, noResults, strikeColor, nonJpTag, muted, scale, prefix) are NOT catalog fields -- they never belong in this file, only in a series entry's own platforms item.

key.description: Stable id, by convention the iconImg filename stem.

imgStyle.description: Raw inline CSS, sizing only by convention. May also carry a `filter:` escape hatch to opt out of the standard light/dark tint (e.g. nintendo-snes uses grayscale to keep its multi-colour logo legible).

name.description: Catalog label: every variant this platform has ever meant, e.g. 'Xbox One (Physical; Digital; Enhanced; Xbox One X Enhanced; 360 Compatibility)'. A series entry never inherits this whole -- only its base label (stripped of a trailing "(...)") via its own `paren`.

jpTag.description: Catalog default "(jp)" marker, overridable per platformGroups item.

nameOverride.description: Marks this key as one where a series entry's own `name` (a full label override, not paren-composed) is legitimate -- e.g. `book`'s entries name a specific medium (Manga/Novel/Short Stories) `paren` can't produce since it can only append to the base label, never replace it. scripts/validate-data.py fails any `name` usage on a key without this flag: `paren` (or nothing) should be enough for every other key -- add the flag here, in the closely-reviewed catalog, rather than looser per-entry `name` usage.

searchSuffix.description: Default suffix word(s) appended after a platforms item's `term` when computing a `search` URL (e.g. fan-movie -> 'game movie', so an entry states only the title). Override per-entry with the item's own `suffix` ('' for no suffix at all).

icon.description: Bootstrap Icons class, alternative to iconImg. No current catalog entry uses this.

text.description: Plain text badge, alternative to iconImg. No current catalog entry uses this.
